artworks.title: Adelasia of Montferrat as Sinope (Castello della Manta)
artworks.description: Baronial-hall fresco at Manta Castle: a medieval lady stands in for Sinope among the female Worthies — the Asopid nymph who tricked Zeus into granting her perpetual virginity, remembered as a Black Sea eponym and a model of shrewd chastity.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus keeps Sinope among Asopus' daughters — the naiad Zeus carried to the Assyrian shore, where she asked for virginity and founded the name of Sinope.

popCulture.title: Asopus
popCulture.description: Among the Asopid sisters who name cities — Sinope the one who outwitted Zeus and gave her name to the Paphlagonian harbour.

popCulture.title: Sinope (mythology)
popCulture.description: Naiad daughter of Asopus — eponym of Sinope on the Black Sea, famous for bargaining eternal virginity from Zeus.
